claim: On the tested CMP 170HX fabric there is no NVLink and no P2P over PCIe Gen2 x4, with about 1.0 GB/s measured bus bandwidth between cards — and this single fact decides the topology choice.
stance_target: the repo's premise that the fabric, not the compute, is what constrains multi-card training topology
scope_conditions: Tested CMP 170HX fabric at PCIe Gen2 x4, no NVLink, no P2P; the Gen2 x4 record predates the club's move to a Gen2 x16 PLX host
quoted_support: The tested CMP 170HX fabric has **no NVLink and no P2P over PCIe Gen2 x4** (about 1.0 GB/s measured bus bandwidth between cards). This one fact decides the topology choice.

claim: Tensor parallelism performs 2 all-reduces per layer, i.e. 86 collectives per forward pass on a 43-layer model, and is communication-bound at every sequence length: TP4 prefill measures flat at ~800 tok/s from 1.5k to 77k tokens.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is a viable training topology on this fabric — the collective count is fixed per layer, so the cost does not amortise over larger batches
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 43 layers, 4x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x4, no P2P
quoted_support: | Tensor parallel | Performs 2 all-reduces per layer (86 collectives per forward pass on a 43-layer model). Communication-bound at every sequence length: prefill measures flat at ~800 tok/s from 1.5k to 77k tokens on TP4 |

claim: Pipeline parallelism moves the payload once per stage boundary (3 hand-offs for 4 stages) and overlaps transfer with compute, putting about 28x less data on the wire than tensor parallelism.
stance_target: the mechanism that makes pipeline parallelism the fabric-appropriate topology, which the repo's 'DDP is the only viable topology' claim omits
scope_conditions: 4-stage pipeline vs 4-way tensor parallel on the same 43-layer model
quoted_support: | Pipeline parallel | Moves the payload once per stage boundary (3 hand-offs for 4 stages) and overlaps transfer with compute: about 28x less data on the wire than TP |
numbers: ~28x less data on the wire than TP

claim: Measured on the same checkpoint and cards, PP beats TP by 6.6x on prefill (5,321 vs 801 tok/s at 77k context) and roughly 2x on aggregate decode; time-to-first-token at 100k context is PP4 14.6 s versus TP4 87.3 s.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is a usable topology at long context on this fabric; the 6.6x prefill gap and 6x TTFT gap at 100k are decisive
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 4x CMP 170HX at Gen2 x4, no P2P, same checkpoint and cards
quoted_support: Measured effect: **PP beats TP by 6.6x on prefill** (5,321 vs 801 tok/s at 77k context) and roughly 2x on aggregate decode, on the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoint and cards. Prefill time-to-first-token at 100k context: PP4 14.6 s vs TP4 87.3 s.
numbers: PP 5,321 tok/s vs TP 801 tok/s at 77k

claim: A healthy unlocked card measures 155.7 TFLOPS fp16, while a card held by the PWRBRK# power brake on PCIe sideband pin B30 measures 39.3 TFLOPS and is capped near 88 W of a 250 W budget with clocks around 1,140 MHz.
stance_target: the repo's ~162 TFLOPS/GPU bf16 compute premise (155.7 TFLOPS fp16 measured is consistent with it), and refutes the 170th-Street spec sheet's 49.05 TFLOPS and the club's own 74.6-78.5 TFLOP/s 'tensor-core gate' figure as descriptions of healthy-card peak
scope_conditions: CMP 170HX, unlocked, healthy vs PWRBRK#-asserted; some workstation boards assert PWRBRK# on x16 slots; check with nvidia-smi -q | grep -A1 'HW Power Brake Slowdown'
quoted_support: **Power-brake (`PWRBRK#`, PCIe sideband pin B30)** is a separate, board-level hazard: some workstation boards assert it on x16 slots, permanently capping a card near 88 W of a 250 W budget and dropping clocks to about 1140 MHz (measured fp16 throughput 39.3 vs 155.7 TFLOPS healthy).

claim: FP8 and FP4 storage formats dequantize fine on SM80 but FP8/FP4 tensor-core compute does not exist there, so DeepGEMM, CuteDSL kernels, Triton fp8e4nv stores and tilelang FP8xFP4 GEMM all fail to compile or run, while AWQ/GPTQ INT4 via Marlin, W8A16, BF16 and flash_attention all work.
stance_target: the repo's claim that GA100 has no FP8 tensor cores, and the corollary that FP8-based training experiments are not runnable on this box
scope_conditions: SM80 / compute capability 8.0, tested across the club's model attempts; FP8 KV cache works via software conversion but costs throughput
quoted_support: SM80 has no FP4 or FP8 tensor-core math. Kernels written for SM89 (Ada FP8) or SM90+ (Hopper, sparse-MLA, FlashInfer fast paths) fail to compile or fail at runtime on SM80. The practical rule: FP8 and FP4 **storage formats** dequantize fine on SM80; FP8/FP4 **tensor-core compute** does not exist here.

claim: FP8 KV cache costs -3.4% decode and -19.5% prefill versus BF16 KV at 131k context on the same server, so FP8 KV buys long context on one card but is not free.
stance_target: whether long-context training or inference on this box can use FP8 KV to fit bigger batches — it can, at a measurable throughput cost
scope_conditions: Qwen3.8-27B, DFlash2 k=7, same server, 131k context, FP8 KV vs BF16 KV
quoted_support: **FP8 KV cost, measured directly (Qwen3.8-27B, DFlash2 k=7, same server):** 131k-context FP8 KV vs BF16 KV: **-3.4% decode** (135.8 vs 140.5 tok/s) and **-19.5% prefill** (1,741 vs 2,161 tok/s).

claim: Speculative-decoding depth must match the checkpoint rather than a rule of thumb: DSpark k=5 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 gives 3.03 mean acceptance and 98.1 tok/s aggregate decode, while k=7 measures worse at 60.3 tok/s because acceptance never extends past about 3 tokens.
stance_target: the hypothesis that a communication-bound box can amortise a fixed per-step cost over a deeper draft — extra drafts beyond the checkpoint's acceptance horizon are pure waste
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 PP4, DSpark, per-position acceptance 0.730/0.569/0.372/0.226/0.131 at k=5
quoted_support: | DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (PP4) | DSpark | 5 | 3.03 (per-position 0.730/0.569/0.372/0.226/0.131) | 98.1 tok/s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (PP4) | DSpark | 7 | 1.43-2.51 | 60.3 tok/s (worse: acceptance never extends past ~3 tokens, so extra drafts are pure waste) |

claim: Independent reports put field failure around 50% among buyers, with faults appearing only above the 8 GiB region a mining rig would ever touch — the cards pass nvidia-smi and die only under a large model's full memory footprint.
stance_target: the reliability risk of building a training program on this hardware: a strict pre-purchase QC gate (memtest_vulkan, vram-gate allocating ~61 GiB) is mandatory rather than optional
scope_conditions: Community field reports on second-hand CMP 170HX cards; club QC procedure requires memtest_vulkan v0.5.0 (~10 min/card) and a vram-gate full-footprint write/verify/burn cycle
quoted_support: **Field failure rate is high above the mining window.** Independent reports put failures around 50% among buyers, and faults appear **only** above the 8 GiB region a mining rig would ever touch; the cards pass `nvidia-smi` and die only under a large model's full memory footprint.

claim: Eager safetensors loading exhausts host RAM: four pipeline ranks loading a 156 GiB checkpoint concurrently, each reading ~3.2 GB shards, OOM-killed workers silently at 7 of 48 shards on a 94 GiB host with no traceback.
stance_target: the host-side memory requirement of any multi-rank training run on this box — checkpoint loading alone can exhaust a 94 GiB host
scope_conditions: Four pipeline ranks, 156 GiB checkpoint, 94 GiB host RAM, --safetensors-load-strategy eager; fix is the default streaming safe_open
quoted_support: Four pipeline ranks loading a 156 GiB checkpoint concurrently, each reading roughly 3.2 GB shards, exhausted a 94 GiB host and the kernel OOM-killed workers silently at 7 of 48 shards (no traceback).

claim: An NCCL store timeout (600 s) during weight load is caused by storage-read skew across ranks, not a network or NCCL defect: one rank stalls on an NFS page-in while its peers reach the rendezvous store first, and torchrun SIGTERMs the stalled rank.
stance_target: a failure mode any distributed training run on this box would hit — it argues for staging weights locally before launching
scope_conditions: NFS-backed weight load, multi-rank torchrun, 600 s NCCL store timeout
quoted_support: | NCCL store timeout (600 s) | One rank stalls on an NFS page-in for a large shard while its peers reach the rendezvous store first; the skew exceeds the store timeout and `torchrun` SIGTERMs the stalled rank | Root cause is storage-read skew across ranks, not a network or NCCL defect; stage weights locally (section e) to remove the skew |
